analysis: The only change in this PR is at StandaloneServerTests.swift line 663. A test-only stub `StandaloneStubLanguageModel.prepare` signature moved from `(input, cache, windowSize: Int?)` to `(input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters)`. This tracks an upstream `LanguageModel` protocol API change. The stub still returns `.tokens(input.text)`, and `newCache` is unchanged. The file is a test target, so it ships no production code and adds no network surface, key handling, attestation, authorization or cache-storage behavior. I also read the rest of the displayed test file (units 5 and 6) for context. It exercises existing controls and is unchanged: bearer-token enforcement on local routes, fixed error envelopes that do not reflect request-derived model IDs, the 32 MiB body ceiling, the CBv2 catalog gate, KV re-slice and unwind ordering, and the SSD cache close on stop. None of these tests weakens an assertion in the diff, and the diff is limited to line 663. Relevant threat entries are T-041 (the SSD prefix cache, only referenced by the stop test) and TB-007 (the inference engine boundary). Neither is altered by this change. Open question for the next pass: the production-side adoption of the new upstream `prepare(state:prefill:)` signature (for example the MLXLMCommon dependency bump and real model adapters) is not in the supplied evidence. That would need review wherever it is changed, since it could affect KV or prefill behavior in T-028 and T-041.
